claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a homogeneous single-phase solid solution without secondary phases or precipitates.
The low hardness and strength of single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are governed primarily by facile dislocation motion.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has low lattice friction.
The crystal structure of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has sufficiently high symmetry to activate multiple slip systems readily.
Activation of multiple slip systems promotes rapid dynamic recovery during deformation.
Dynamic recovery in this alloy occurs through dislocation annihilation or rearrangement.
Multiple slip, cross-slip, dislocation annihilation, and dynamic recovery prevent dislocation pile-up in the alloy.
Low lattice friction and high crystal symmetry cause rapid dislocation motion and effective dynamic recovery.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and effective dynamic recovery minimize strain hardening.
Reduced pile-up and strain hardening result in low hardness and yield strength.
In situ TEM under the stated loading conditions will reveal widespread, diffuse dislocation motion.
In situ TEM will reveal minimal formation of dislocation pile-ups.
Nanoindentation and bulk tensile testing will show modest hardness and low strain-hardening rates.
A lack of substantial obstacles to dislocation glide will correlate with the alloy's low hardness and strength.
Lowering the deformation temperature will suppress dynamic recovery.
Suppressing dynamic recovery at lower temperature should increase dislocation pile-up density, yield strength, and strain hardening.
The proposed mechanism applies at room temperature and strain rates from 10^-3 to 10^-1 s^-1 when the alloy remains a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as cast and homogenized, whereas the baseline is described as as-cast. These are distinct processing states unless the baseline is also homogenized, which is not stated.
